pamphlet_excerpts: Brief Descriptions: From the brief descriptions in this pamphlet, you have learnedsome of the difficulties American Indian tribes faced after thearrival of Europeans.
Native Peoples Lost: Native peoples lost so much that by thelate 19th and early 20th centuries, it seemed to some observersthat they must be doomed.
Others Lost Huge: Others lost huge numbersof their people and all of their lands and possessions.
Mission Indians California: Some, like the Mission Indians of California, lost cultural memories, their Indian ways of living and s­ urviving, after being undermissionary.
step_by_step_procedure: People Predicted Eventually: Some people predicted that eventually all Indian culturesand their traditional ways would be lost and that finally the Indians themselves.
Native Peoples Endured: Native peoples endured, and today there are about 2 million American Indians living in the United States.
Today Than Half: Today, more than half of American Indians live outsidethe reservations that were set aside for them by the federalgovernment.
Live Big Cities: Many live in big cities; others live in smallercommunities and rural areas.

pamphlet_excerpts: Indians Relearning Lost: Indians are relearning lost traditions and languages and revivingtheir arts and crafts, their songs, dances, and stories.
Havechosen Not Disappear: Many havechosen not to disappear into America’s “melting pot.” Indians are reclaiming control over what happens to them.
They Want Decide: They want to decide for themselves how they will live in themodern world.
Question They Cultural: The question is, how can they keep cultural roots aliveand protect and preserve tribal identities, yet still be a part ofmodern society?.
step_by_step_procedure: There Easy Answer: There is no easy answer, and no one knowswhat the future holds.
History American Indians: The history of American Indians is filled with the names ofmen and women who are remembered for deeds that set themapart from others.
They Renowned Leaders: They may have been renowned leaders, peacemakers, or lawmakers.
Pocahontas Sacajawea: Some, like Pocahontas, Sacajawea, Hahyonhwatha (known as “Hiawatha”), and Tecumseh, livedcenturies ago.

pamphlet_excerpts: Youtake Journey Discovery: This pamphlet will help youtake that important first step in your journey of discovery.
Usethe Information Here: Usethe information here as a starting point to learn more about American Indians and Ameri­can heritage.
Want Focus Tribe: You might want to focus on only one tribe to fulfill all ofthe merit badge requirements.
Want Learn Moreabout: You might want to learn moreabout Indian life in general before Euro­peans came, as well asafter they arrived.
step_by_step_procedure: Investigate Indians Liveand: You might also investigate how Indians liveand work today and carry on their ancient traditions.
Ask School Public: Ask your school or public librarian for booksand other materials about different Indian groups.
Anatural History Museum: If you have anatural history museum in your area, ask the curator or personin charge for information.
Town City American: See if your town or city has an American Indian center, oran Indian tribal council or similar governing group.

pamphlet_excerpts: Indians Relearning Lost: Indians are relearning lost traditions and languages and revivingtheir arts and crafts, their songs, dances, and stories.
Havechosen Not Disappear: Many havechosen not to disappear into America’s “melting pot.” Indians are reclaiming control over what happens to them.
They Want Decide: They want to decide for themselves how they will live in themodern world.
Question They Cultural: The question is, how can they keep cultural roots aliveand protect and preserve tribal identities, yet still be a part ofmodern society?.
step_by_step_procedure: There Easy Answer: There is no easy answer, and no one knowswhat the future holds.
History American Indians: The history of American Indians is filled with the names ofmen and women who are remembered for deeds that set themapart from others.
They Renowned Leaders: They may have been renowned leaders, peacemakers, or lawmakers.
Pocahontas Sacajawea: Some, like Pocahontas, Sacajawea, Hahyonhwatha (known as “Hiawatha”), and Tecumseh, livedcenturies ago.

fields.Requirement & Topic: Req 5 - Visit a museum either in-person
fields.Primary Standard: Visit a museum either in-person or virtually to see American Indian exhibitions and collections. Discuss with your counselor what you observed or learned from two exhibitions and identify 10 artifacts by tribe or nation, their shape, size, and use.
fields.Field Evidence Recorded: Completed structured workbook organizer with specific examples, dates, and Indian Lore terminology.
fields.Safety & Verification: Reviewed against Official Scouting America Indian Lore Merit Badge Pamphlet (p. 37, p. 92) and verified during counselor conference.
